title: What can you say about folate in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 7 wordings for folate; the strongest is "Helps form red blood cells" (strong, 30-1,000 µg folic acid a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents birth defects, or reduces the risk of neural tube defects or spina bifida".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU (normal blood formation) after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 30-1,000 µg a day for adults 19 and older (30-800 µg at 14 to 18), counted as micrograms of folic acid, not dietary folate equivalents (DFE). EU: at least 30 µg, 15% of the 200 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). 1,000 µg a day is the ODS upper limit for folic acid from supplements and fortified foods.
supported_wordings.form: Folic acid or L-5-methyltetrahydrofolate (or its calcium or glucosamine salt)

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents birth defects, or reduces the risk of neural tube defects or spina bifida
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names birth defects. In the US this is FDA's authorized health claim (21 CFR 101.79), with set wording and conditions (see fda_health_claims); Health Canada's version is a Canada only note.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Supports healthy brain and spinal cord development in the baby
wordings_to_avoid.why: FDA's folate health claim names 'birth defects of the brain or spinal cord' (21 CFR 101.79(c)(2)(i)(C)), so this wording reads as that claim without its required conditions.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers homocysteine to protect the heart, or reduces the risk of heart disease or stroke
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases. FDA's qualified claim on folic acid, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12 and vascular disease has set wording (see fda_health_claims).
Names a mental health disorder; the supported EU wording is normal psychological function.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
